govdocs-archive_org-nsia-AlvarezLuisDr_D: This item — Dr. Luis Alvarez — is a National Security Internet Archive file on the Nobel physicist. Alvarez studied the JFK assassination evidence. His physics backed the lone-gunman theory. Researchers value such files. The item is a fragment of the assassination record.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonso-rodrig: A 1913 entry on St. Alonso Rodriguez — the Jesuit lay brother of Majorca. Thomas Slater honors his humble sanctity. Forty years a porter, he counseled saints. His door opened to heaven. The doorkeeper saint of the Society. His feast crowns the October calendar.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonzo-coello: A 1913 entry on Alonso Sánchez Coello — the court painter of Philip II. George Williamson honors his portraits. His kings and queens gaze from the Prado. The Spanish court lives in his art. A master of royal likeness. His Infanta portraits charm the Prado visitors.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonzo-sanche: This 1913 reference article on Alonso Sánchez — the Jesuit missionary of the East. Philip Finegan sketches his career. His voyages spanned the Spanish empire. The entry honors his zeal. A soldier of the missions. His missions reached the Philippine shores.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-ferna: This 1913 reference piece on Antonio Fernandez — a name in the church story. F.M. Rudge records what is known. The entry preserves his modest fame. The old registers keep his name. A figure of the ecclesiastical past. His name survives in the archives.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-balthazar-alv: This 1913 reference piece on Balthazar Alvarez — the Jesuit director of St. Teresa. Thomas Campbell honors his guiding hand. He steered the mystic's early years. The reform's trials tested him too. A confessor of the saints. His counsels steadied the reform's course.
